items.title: Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1：评估科研工作流中的 AI 智能体
items.description: 斯坦福大学研究人员领衔发布 Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1，用来自生命、物理、地球、数学和工程科学的 70 个专家精选任务评估 AI 智能体的科研能力。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.virxact.com/items/cmtcxdp3f07l3roq5uk6om1aw
items.author: noreply@aihot.virxact.com (Hacker News 热门（buzzing.cc 中文翻译）)
items.content: 斯坦福大学研究人员领衔发布 Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1，用来自生命、物理、地球、数学和工程科学的 70 个专家精选任务评估 AI 智能体的科研能力。 70 个专家任务里最强模型仅解决 30%，成本与 token 前沿还显示不同系统取舍，为选择科学智能体提供了比软件基准更接近真实研究的依据。 Terminal-Bench-Science 在研究人员自身的工作流程上评估 AI 智能体。为 AI 的科学能力设定标准的，是科学家，而不是模型开发者或数据供应商。 Terminal-Bench-Science 是一项由斯坦福大学研究人员牵头、由 Terminal-Bench 团队构建的基准测试，并与来自全球多个科学学科和研究机构的领域专家合作完成。它通过一系列来自科学研究、由专家精心挑选的多样化挑战性工作流程，来衡量 AI 智能体的能力。 Terminal-Bench-Science 是一个持续演进的基准测试，与前沿 AI 同步发展，在科学需求与 AI 开发之间形成反馈循环。我们的首个版本包含来自生命科学、物理科学、地球科学、数学和工程科学的 70 项任务。目前评估过的最强模型 Claude Opus 5，在 Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 上达到了 30% 的解决率。 尽管 Terminal-Bench 推动了软件工程领域 AI 智能体的进步，Terminal-Bench-Science 则将同样的雄心带到了科学领域。我们的目标是推动具备科学能力的智能体发展，使其成为有用的研究助手。这些智能体应能执行技术要求高且耗时的流程，让科学家得以将更多时间投入到科学中人类判断最为关键的部分：定义研究问题、形成假设、解释和验证结果，以及传播研究发现。在这一角色中，AI 智能体可以拓展研究人员所能取得的成果，并帮助加速科学发现。

items.title: OpenAI：ChatGPT 广告年化收入运行率已达 10 亿美元
items.description: IT之家 8 月 31 日消息，OpenAI 当地时间周一宣布，其广告业务的年化收入运行率（annualized revenue run rate，是将企业短期已确认收入按当前速度外推至全年的估算指标）已经达到 10 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 67.36 亿元人民币） 。该公司将这一里程碑视为其“多元化商业模式”取得成效的证明。 这家人工智能公司正在为预计规模庞大的首次公开募股（IPO）做准备，同时也面临着向投资者证明其 8,520 亿美元 （现汇率约合 5.74 万亿元人民币） 估值合理性的压力。OpenAI 表示，旗下广告业务发展至今约 200 天，是在企业服务、消费者订阅以及按使用量计费的应用程序接口（API）等现有收入来源基础上的又一增长引擎。 OpenAI 于今年 2 月开始在美国测试 ChatGPT 内的广告功能。这一决定此前备受期待，但同时也引发了不小争议。 数字广告长期以来一直是谷歌和 Meta 等大型科技公司的重要收入来源。不过，OpenAI 进军广告业务的举动也遭到了主要竞争对手 Anthropic 的嘲讽，后者甚至将 OpenAI 推进广告业务作为其首个超

items.title: 沙特 13 岁以上公民和居民可免费使用 Adobe 两项服务 1 年，总价超 40 亿美元
items.description: IT之家 8 月 31 日消息，Adobe 当地时间今日在沙特阿拉伯首都利雅得举行的 LEAP 2026 大会上宣布，沙特 13 岁以上公民和居民将 获得 Adobe Firefly Standard 及 Adobe Express Premium 的 12 个月免费使用权 。 这是 Adobe 与沙特通信和信息技术部、沙特主权财富基金 PIF 旗下人工智能企业 HUMAIN 扩展合作的一部分，覆盖超 2700 万沙特人，总价值超过 40 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 269.43 亿元人民币） 。 Adobe 同时宣布自今天起在全球范围内的 Adobe Express 桌面版、网页版和 iOS 版上 提供现代标准阿拉伯语（从右到左）语言支持 ，包括排版、文本编辑、用户界面控件以及一系列专为沙特文化量身定制的模板。 此外，HUMAIN 和 Adobe 即将联合推出一款图像模型。该模型能根据沙特公民和创意团队的文化背景、视觉参考、创意需求生成高质量的图像。

items.description: IT之家 8 月 31 日消息，NVIDIA（英伟达）与联发科技 (Mediatek) 今日宣布深化长期合作伙伴关系，共同打造跨世代的 AI 基础设施、边缘 AI 运算、车用产品。 联发科技将采用 NVIDIA NVLink Fusion 平台为客户开发客制化 XPU 芯片 ，整合至 NVIDIA 机柜级系统及 AI 工厂。NVIDIA 同时向联发科技发行的海外可转换公司债投资 35 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 235.75 亿元人民币） 。 此外， 双方将持续合作开发未来数代 RTX Spark / DGX Spark 电脑芯片 ；两家企业也将持续开放具备 AI 功能的 SDV（软件定义汽车）平台。 NVIDIA 创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋表示： AI 正在重新定义所有计算平台，涵盖从全球大型 AI 工厂到个人电脑与汽车等领域。联发科技是全球领先的半导体公司之一，在 SoC 设计、连接技术以及高性能与高能效方面拥有深厚实力。透过更深度的合作，我们正共同打造能将 NVIDIA 加速计算技术拓展至更多新市场的平台，并让客户得以大规模建构具差异化优势的 AI 系统。 联发科技副董事长兼

items.title: 谷歌 AI 应用 Dreambeans 取消订阅制，开放免费测试
items.description: IT之家 8 月 31 日消息，据科技媒体 MacObserver 今天报道，谷歌 AI 应用 Dreambeans 现已取消付费订阅要求， 并在美国开放免费测试 。 据官方介绍，Dreambeans 是一款高度个性化的信息流应用，它不会让用户无限向下浏览内容， 而是每天早晨提供数量有限的 AI 插图式新闻 。 IT之家了解到，Dreambeans 依托用户的谷歌相关数据生成各类推荐内容。谷歌官方介绍：“在获得用户授权后，Dreambeans 依托个人智能技术，整合 Gmail、日历、谷歌相册、YouTube、搜索记录等谷歌应用信息，每日精选有限条数的生活随笔，帮用户迸发新鲜灵感。” 举几个例子：部分内容是地理位置推荐，比如推荐用户住所周边一家合口味的新晋咖啡馆；就像宣传视频演示的那样，若用户在谷歌日历里备注了即将领养小狗，Dreambeans 就会推送饲养幼犬的相关科普内容；还有一部分内容，会依据用户过往的兴趣偏好，从全网筛选合适的资讯文章。 该应用最初仅限 Google AI Ultra 订阅用户使用，如今面向普通用户开放，开发团队希望借此收集更多反馈。

items.title: 欧盟委员会认定 ChatGPT、Reddit、Roblox“超大型”身份，收紧监管
items.description: IT之家 8 月 31 日消息，欧盟委员会当地时间 8 月 31 日宣布，依据《数字服务法》（DSA），正式认定 ChatGPT、Reddit 及 Roblox 为监管对象。 欧盟委员会表示， 上述服务在欧盟境内的月均活跃用户数已达 4500 万人以上 ，达到法定的认定门槛；将 ChatGPT 认定为超大型在线搜索引擎，并将 Reddit 与 Roblox 认定为超大型在线平台。 IT之家注：根据《数字服务法》，一旦被列入超大型在线平台或超大型在线搜索引擎名单， 相关企业就必须遵守欧盟规定的一系列更严格的规则和义务 ，包括风险评估、内容审核、透明度报告以及其他监管要求。 欧盟委员会称，ChatGPT 属于人工智能系统，能够与用户交互并响应其提示词和查询请求（包括执行网络检索）。因此 ChatGPT 属于混合型服务，在 DSA 框架下构成了在线搜索引擎。 收到认定通知后，相关平台有四个月的过渡期（即截至 2026 年 12 月底），以满足 DSA 针对超大型在线平台与超大型在线搜索引擎设立的附加合规要求。 此前，Roblox、Reddit 和 ChatGPT 已分别受限于 DSA 针对普

items.title: 豆包辟谣“建议开水煮拖鞋”传闻：博主故意引导回复，玩梗视频未披露虚构情节
items.description: IT之家 8 月 31 日消息，豆包公关负责人刘星今日在微博发文，回应近期在互联网传播的“豆包建议煮拖鞋”流言。 据IT之家了解，近日多个平台出现一批博主发文称，自己的拖鞋暴晒变形后向豆包求助恢复办法，结果豆包建议将拖鞋放在锅里用开水煮，导致拖鞋和锅都煮坏了。 刘星表示，豆包实际上并不会给出这样的回复。大家自己问一下豆包就知道，在关于“拖鞋被暴晒怎么处理”的问题上， 豆包会明确提醒不要相信开水烫 、 蒸煮的偏方 。 经官方核实，这类视频是基于一个“是谁说的晒小的鞋能煮回来”的视频段子改编。官方也联系到了最早发布“豆包建议煮拖鞋”的视频博主，对方承认， 是故意引导豆包按照要求的错误内容进行回复 ， 摆拍制作成玩梗视频传播 。因为流量不错，后续不少账号进行了同质化的摆拍。 这些视频并没有标注是虚构玩梗摆拍 ，导致部分媒体、机构账号信以为真，转发了这类谣言内容。一条谣言变成了“新闻”。

items.description: IT之家 8 月 31 日消息，据 The Information 报道，OpenAI 近几个月购买了数万台苹果 Mac mini 和 Mac Studio 电脑，用于训练能够操作计算机的 AI 系统。 这些 Mac 并非用于 OpenAI 基础模型的大规模预训练，而是主要承担强化学习任务。在这一训练过程中，AI 智能体需要在真实计算机环境中反复练习完成各种操作任务。 据了解，OpenAI 购买的主要是配备大容量统一内存的 Mac 产品，并利用这些设备运行与“计算机操作型 AI 智能体”相关的模型和训练工作负载。 这类硬件能够为 AI 模型提供真实的计算机操作环境，使其学习如何浏览软件界面、与应用程序互动以及完成各种电脑任务。通过这样的环境，AI 智能体可以反复进行训练和评估。 OpenAI 如此大规模采购 Mac，也反映出整个 AI 行业对于大内存苹果电脑的需求正在快速增长。 目前，配备大容量内存的 Mac mini 和 Mac Studio 已经变得较难购买，部分型号甚至连续数月处于缺货状态。AI 公司尤其看重这些配置，原因在于苹果的统一内存架构允许 CPU 和 GPU 访问同一个

items.title: 亚马逊 AWS 加码政府 AI 赛道，OpenAI、Meta、Anthropic 等大模型集体登陆 GovCloud
items.description: IT之家 8 月 31 日消息，亚马逊云服务（AWS）昨天宣布，公司已扩大 GovCloudAI 模型可用范围， 美国的政府机构可通过 Amazon Bedrock 渠道 ， 使用 Anthropic、OpenAI、Meta 等公司旗下 AI 大模型 ，以及亚马逊自家的 Nova 模型。 据悉，AWS GovCloud 专门面向美国政府机构，旨在提供符合政府监管、安全和外部隔离的云计算环境。 亚马逊对此表示：“我们欣然宣布，AWS GovCloud（美国）现可以通过 Amazon Bedrock 提供多种 AI 模型，为政府客户、国防工业和技术合作伙伴提供各种 AI 模型。” 亚马逊 AWS 业务当今正保持强势增长。2026 年第二季度，AWS 营业利润同比增长 63%，营收同比增长 37%，AI 和芯片业务的强劲表现是推动增长的重要因素。 亚马逊管理层预计，AWS 的营收最终可能达到 1 万亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 6.74 万亿元人民币） 。目前全球约 85% 的 IT 支出仍用于本地部署（on-premises）环境，这意味着云计算市场仍拥有较大的增长空间。

items.title: The U.S. is building barriers around drones and robots, but China has scale to get around them
items.description: The U.S. is shutting out more foreign-made drones and robots. China’s scale means the global competition may simply move elsewhere.
items.author: Kate Park
items.content: In July and August, Washington tightened restrictions on foreign-made advanced robotic systems and imposed steep tariffs on imported drones and their components, both moves citing national-security concerns. The drone tariffs take effect in September, with additional component tariffs following in 2027. These moves are part of a broader U.S. effort to restrict foreign technology in strategically important industries. The FCC’s Covered List , established in 2021, initially targeted telecommunications and surveillance equipment from companies including Huawei, ZTE and Hikvision before expanding to foreign-made drones and, most recently, to advanced robotic devices. The latest move comes as Chinese manufacturers have built commanding positions in both drones and humanoid robots, often competing at prices U.S. and European rivals struggle to match. Taken together, the restrictions are raising a bigger question for the global robotics industry: If Chinese drones and humanoids are increasingly shut out of the U.S., where does the competition move next? The restrictions may protect parts of the American market, but they don’t directly address China’s global manufacturing scale and cost advantages. Industry analysts and executives who spoke with TechCrunch said the result may be less a clean U.S.-China split than a more fragmented global market, with Chinese companies expanding elsewhere while U.S. and allied manufacturers compete in markets where security requirements matter more.

items.description: Sandhya Devanathan will oversee some OpenAI operations across Southeast Asia and Australia in her new role.
items.author: Jagmeet Singh
items.content: Meta’s India and Southeast Asia vice president, Sandhya Devanathan, is leaving the social media giant to join OpenAI, the ChatGPT maker told TechCrunch. Devanathan will be based in Singapore and report to OpenAI’s Asia-Pacific managing director, Kiran Mani. She will oversee consumer growth, enterprise adoption and partnerships, regulatory engagement, and operations across Southeast Asia and Australia, OpenAI said. The executive is leaving Meta after more than a decade at the company, which has been the subject of growing scrutiny over issues such as online safety and content moderation. Devanathan was involved in the company’s decision process in the country, a person familiar with the matter said. Devanathan’s appointment comes days after Prabhjeet Singh joined OpenAI as its India head. Singh had spent more than a decade at Uber, where he led its India and South Asia business. OpenAI has been expanding its presence across the Asia Pacific, opening offices in Singapore, Tokyo, Seoul, Sydney, and Delhi over the past two years. Following Devanathan’s departure, Meta’s India managing director, Arun Srinivas, will report directly to Benjamin Joe, the company’s vice president for Asia Pacific, a person familiar with the matter told TechCrunch.

items.title: Hugging Face is selling a cute $399 open source duck robot, Microduck
items.description: Clem Delangue, CEO of Hugging Face, said the Microduck is an “open-source robot you can teach new tricks with reinforcement learning.”
items.author: Rebecca Bellan
items.content: Hugging Face unveiled the Microduck on Thursday, a cute little duck-like robot that sells for $399 — and ships before Christmas. Clem Delangue, CEO of Hugging Face, said the Microduck is an “open-source robot you can teach new tricks with reinforcement learning.” The 25-centimeter-tall duck can waddle, pick things up with its beak, get back up when it falls, crouch, and even roller skate. “Welcome to the era of open-source affordable robots to democratize physical AI and world models!” Delangue said. Hugging Face is best known as a platform and community where developers go for open model weights. However, the company acquired French startup Pollen Robotics in April 2025 to build affordable, open source AI hardware. A couple of months later, the two launched Reachy Mini , a small desktop robot . Today, they sell the $499 Reachy Mini, which is powered by a Raspberry Pi computer, and the $399 Reachy Mini Lite, powered by a Mac or PC. The new Microduck perceives the world with a camera, lidar sensors, and two IMUs (inertial measurement units that measure and report an object’s movement). Pollen Robotics noted that the Microduck’s behaviors can be trained in simulation and directly deployed on the robot. Developers can then fine-tune the bot, retrain it, and redeploy it. The SDK (software development kit), simulation, and full RL training stack are available on GitHub.

items.title: AI’s memory crunch is coming for Android apps
items.description: Google is setting new memory-use limits for Android apps as AI data centers contribute to hardware shortages that could leave lower-cost phones with less memory.
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: Google is making changes to its requirements for Android apps as developers face industrywide memory chip shortages driven by the AI data center boom. This week, the tech giant announced two new app quality requirements, one of which is focused on reducing apps’ memory usage and optimizing its code. The company explains that the mobile industry is now facing “significant hardware supply constraints that are altering device memory availability,” which can then, in turn, affect the consumer’s experience with their devices. To address this, Google is now establishing new performance thresholds across several areas, like dynamic memory usage and bitmap usage. In addition, Google is adding code optimization requirements designed to prevent things like app slowdowns and crashes related to performance. To aid developers, the company is rolling out new tools that will alert them when their apps exceed the new thresholds so they can take action by optimizing their code. More diagnostic tools will arrive later in the year, Google noted, including deeper insights provided by a Memory Limiter feature that prevents apps from using too much device memory. The changes are meant to help Android app and game makers continue to deliver a quality experience, Google says, while reflecting a market where memory may not be as widely available, particularly for low-end devices where price points are a concern. items.author: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai
items.content: In July, OpenAI admitted that one of its agents tasked with completing a cybersecurity experiment broke out of containment and hacked AI dataset platform Hugging Face. That incident, which got a full accounting from OpenAI yesterday, was the first publicly reported case where an LLM went rogue and autonomously hacked a third party. Since then, that unprecedented sci-fi-esque event turned out to be far less rare than anyone would hope for. According to a satirical website called Felony Bench (for benchmark), which tallies these incidents, there have been 17 incidents in total. It’s important to remember that criminal law experts are not entirely sure whether the AI companies that made the LLMs that did the hacking can be prosecuted, nor whether the victims can sue them. But we are likely going to get an answer to those questions soon . Anthropic and OpenAI models lead the race with eight incidents each, and Meta trails behind with one, according to the site. items.title: OpenAI cuts out SpaceX-owned Cursor
items.description: PLUS: Submit your iOS app to the App Store with Codex
items.content: Good morning, AI enthusiasts, and welcome to our 9,208 new readers. Sam Altman and Elon Musk have fought over companies, lawsuits, talent, and more. Now the feud is landing somewhere developers may actually feel it… One of the most popular AI coding editors on the market. OpenAI's models will exit the newly SpaceX-owned Cursor by mid-November, with Musk's record on past agreements as the dealbreaker. Elon’s response? He “couldn’t care less.” The Rundown: OpenAI just announced that it will be removing its models from coding platform Cursor by Nov.12, coming after the company was acquired by SpaceX last month — citing Elon Musk’s history of violating contracts as the reason for the decision. OAI said it stretched the wind-down as far as its contract allows via cancellation rights that opened once Cursor was sold, calling the decision “incredibly tough.” OAI's evidence includes the $2M-a-year tweet deal Musk killed after buying Twitter, plus xAI training on its outputs, which Musk called “partly” true. Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown reaffirmed support for Cursor, with many calling out the company’s similar move against Windsurf over its potential OAI acquisition.

items.title: Inside Meta's $18B teen crackdown
items.description: PLUS: Scientists make cookies out of plastic
items.content: Good morning, tech enthusiasts. Meta agreed to radically reshape Facebook and Instagram for teens as part of an $18B settlement over claims its platforms harmed young users — and now it’s trying to make sure TikTok and YouTube get dragged into the same future. Also today: Apple is finally ready to launch its first foldable iPhone, while scientists figure out how to turn plastic waste into edible cookies. The Rundown: Meta’s $18B teen-safety settlement comes with a twist: $5.3B only lands if TikTok and YouTube accept the same restrictions and pay ~$6B each. Meta has now taken out full-page newspaper ads to make sure its rivals know exactly what it wants. The settlement resolves claims from dozens of U.S. states that Meta designed Facebook and Instagram to keep children hooked while downplaying the risks. Teen accounts will face a 2-hour daily limit, an overnight shutdown, muted school-hour notifications, stronger age checks, and break prompts. Meta guaranteed about $12.7B of the settlement, while another ~$5.3B is tied to TikTok and YouTube adopting comparable teen-safety restrictions and payments.

items.title: Every machine is about to speak Claude
items.description: PLUS: Use these AI skills to make better decisions quickly
items.content: Good morning, AI enthusiasts, and welcome to our 2,879 new readers. Anthropic’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) started as a connector and eventually became the default way AI agents talk to software. The company’s next act is getting a bit more physical. The new Model Hardware Standard plugs agents into the microscopes, robot arms, and assembly lines the world already runs, a simple layer that could suddenly make every machine AI-ready. The Rundown: Anthropic just introduced the Model Hardware Standard in research preview, which lets AI agents look up, learn, and run factory machines like microscopes, robotic arms, and other lab gear that previously needed custom code — built to spread in an industry-standard way similar to the company’s Model Context Protocol (MCP). Anthropic claims setup times of “hours or minutes” under the new spec, down from the weeks specialists currently spend hand-wiring instruments. Machine owners describe their equipment in natural language, with MHS turning it into a reference file agents can read to learn how to operate the device. In one test, Claude taught itself to align a laser by trial and error, then simplified the routine into a script that automated the job in a single pass.

items.title: Cyborg roaches become tiny paramedics
items.description: PLUS: Softbank eyes 1X in $6B deal
items.content: Good morning, robotics enthusiasts. Somewhere in a Brisbane lab, a cockroach is learning to administer drugs. Six months after cyborg roaches debuted as disaster-zone scouts, University of Queensland engineers have promoted them — strapping a camera to one bug, a remote-triggered injector to another, and rebranding the pair as search-and-rescue “paraborgs.” Also today: Amazon looks for new ways to replace people with robots, and 1X’s NEO humanoid may fall into SoftBank’s hands. The Rundown: Six months after we covered cyborg cockroaches being turned into reconnaissance scouts, researchers have pushed the idea in a wild direction — giving the insects cameras and injectors to find and treat people trapped in disaster zones . University of Queensland engineers have bolted cameras and remote-triggered drug injectors onto giant burrowing cockroaches, producing “paraborgs.” In tests, the bugs delivered injections 95% of the time when already within 15 cm of a target, while the full navigate-position-inject sequence worked in 72% of trials. One roach carries the camera, another carries the needle, and a human triggers it; UQ engineer Thang Vo-Doan predicts rescue swarms are 5-10 years off.
